realizes.rationale: Holds the two selections that start in the tree, and each is made only when the reader uses a control: a row goes through the one subject selection, which the read cache answers when it holds the subject, and a kept family's continuation control selects that family. Nothing else reads for a kept family.

Hands the rail the walk and the mark computed among the walked families, and hands the reading area the mark computed among the answer's own families and the answer itself, so nothing of a kept family reaches the reading area.

The effect that answers a focus request. It leaves the request alone unless the render's tree intent is later than the one the request recorded; it marks the request answered when such a render sees a new answer; while the subject is pending it returns, and a read that has ended failed or refused calls `revealUnavailableRead`, which reveals the status on the stacked layout without spending the request; a `scrollOnly` request waits until it is answered; then it clears the request and lands the focus.

Holds diff layout, full-file disclosure and the open expression path as workspace-level state, with full-file off so changed regions show by default; it remembers the element that opened an expression, and closePath(null) returns focus to that opener.

Keeps the reader's chosen family as the mark when it is among the families it is given: the walked tree's for the rail, the answer's own for the reading area. A kept family's row is a row of the tree and not of the answer, so the rail's mark needs the wider list.
Renders the requested subject's pending state or its failure/refusal inside the reading area while the rest of the workspace keeps its DOM.
This function makes the reveal for a failed or refused read, and only when the guard and the stacked in-tree test both hold.

Composes the walked FamilyRailContext as ReviewNavigation’s child, passes walkedEntries and lane summary counts, and exposes comparison-page/worklist destinations. The navigation has no listLoaded prop or separate catalogue-return rail; the valid FamilyRailContext composition and traversal disabling while the change-set page is open remain.

Advances the walk with every answer the workspace shows and gives the rail the walked families. It computes two selection marks: for the rail among the walked families, so a kept family's row can carry the mark, and for the reading area among the answer's own families. While the subject is unanswered only the reader's explicit choice is marked, so the mark stays on the requested row. The cases "keeps every row when a selected subject is refused, and starts afresh at the offer of the task context" and "keeps every row when the read of a selected subject fails" of `dashboard/src/panels/review/ReviewSurface.walkFresh.test.tsx` test the unanswered states.

Any other request first tests the reader-moved guard (`selectionFocusAvailable`). A `scrollOnly` request (a refresh) only brings the selected node into view, with `block: 'nearest'`, and moves no focus. Any other request calls `focusSelectedRead`, which on the stacked layout reveals the reading area for an in-tree selection and otherwise only moves focus.
It forwards the held lane into the main reading facts.
It composes the navigation controls and destinations in the rail and contains no source-file explorer.

Builds what the tree draws from the walk: the walked families; for each kept family the label of the subject it was last read for (the catalogue's label, else what the answer itself calls that subject); the walk's notice; and, for an answer that composed no family context, the sentence that states this for the selected subject.
Holds the tree intent: a number that goes up with every selection and the flag whether that selection keeps the tree. `beginSelection` is the only writer, and the initial intent does not keep.

Resolves a click on a family row or member row against the families the tree shows, a kept family's included. A family click hands navigation.onSelect the family subject, and a member click hands it the invariant subject keyed by the member row's canonical invariant_id, with the clicked selection passed alongside and the mark that the selection keeps the tree. In both cases the clicked family and revision stay stored as the workspace selection.

For a non-scrollOnly selection request, the moved-focus guard runs before reveal, so a late answer neither takes focus nor scrolls. The separate scrollOnly refresh branch scrolls without moving focus, matching the governing record's explicit refresh exclusion.

The moved-focus predicate guards non-scrollOnly answered selections and unavailable reveals, so those callers neither take focus nor scroll after the reader moves on. The scrollOnly refresh branch is separate and does not call this predicate.
The effect tells a read on its way from one that ended unavailable and calls the reveal for the second without using up the focus request.

Focuses the review center with preventScroll and then explicitly scrolls it into view aligned at block start, so keyboard focus lands on the existing center without relying on the browser's default focus scroll.

Looks the clicked family up among the families the tree shows, a kept family's included, and hands the navigation the row's subject with `keepTree: true`: the family for a family row, the member's canonical invariant for a member row. It is the one handler of a tree row, of a member opened from the reading area and, through the traversal's click, of `j`, `k` and the two visible controls.

The request a selection or a refresh leaves: the element that had focus, the number of the tree intent current when it was made (`after`), whether it only scrolls (`scrollOnly`), and whether an answer has arrived since (`answered`). The effect decides on these fields alone.

Draws the tree whenever the answer composed family context or the walk holds a family, with the answer's own context for the context details and the walked tree for the rows. Kept families therefore stay on screen when the selected subject's answer composes no family context.

Retains one reading-area DOM column for the workspace lifetime. Pending/failed/refused reads show their own status; the worklist flag selects LeafWorklistView; otherwise it shows open context notes, the selected subject’s FamilyReviewCenter, main facts and roster-page note. There is no focused unexplained-lane reader in this column.

Lands a completed selection’s focus only if the reader has not moved it. The target-state notice is found anywhere in the workspace (currently rendered in the main content), else the selected tree node, else the center. A stacked in-tree read reveals the center without moving focus off its row; failed/refused reads reveal status without consuming the pending focus request.
This function decides between the stacked in-tree reveal and the original focus call, from the tree intent and the 60rem media query.

Its `rosterNext` decides what a continuation control does. For a family in the selected subject's context it asks a page of the review on screen. For a kept family it selects the family with `keepTree: true` and the cursor as the selection's page, because the server continues a cursor only for a subject whose context holds the family.
